land.text: the mainland kingdom, restored to Ferdinand on the Bourbon Restoration of 20 May 1815

predecessors.note: The Napoleonic kingdom (Murat) ended in May 1815 in the dossier kingdom-of-naples-napoleonic; Cliopatria's Two Sicilies row starts in 1815.

land.text: Sicily, where Ferdinand had kept his throne in exile

predecessors.note: The kingdom-of-naples-bourbon dossier has the Bourbons keeping Sicily through the Napoleonic years; the island was 'fully reintegrated into the new state' in 1816 (Two Sicilies page).

land.text: the whole of the former kingdom, annexed to the Kingdom of Sardinia and merged into the Kingdom of Italy proclaimed 17 March 1861

successors.note: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Sardinia row for 1861 already draws the south (235,522 km2). Kingdom of Italy page: proclaimed 17 March 1861.

capitals.name: Naples
capitals.note: Inferred: the page gives no capital before 1816; the infobox begins with Palermo (1816-1817) and Naples (1817-1861).

capitals.name: Palermo
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Palermo (1816-1817)'; the page does not say whether 1817 was the year of the move.

rulers.name: Ferdinand I
rulers.note: Table: 12 December 1816 to 4 January 1825 as Ferdinand I of the Two Sicilies; the dossier counts from the 1815 restoration (infobox 'Bourbon Restoration: 20 May 1815'), when he was restored in Naples.

rulers.name: Francis II
rulers.note: 22 May 1859 to 20 March 1861 (table); the siege of Gaeta ended with his surrender in February 1861.

keyframe_review.note: 91,430 km2 for the mainland and Sicily against the infobox 111,900 km2 for 1860 (ratio 0.82, within a factor of two; the infobox year is 1860, when the kingdom was still whole). The state is the Bourbon Restoration of 20 May 1815, named 'Two Sicilies' on 8 December 1816 ('Founded: 8 December 1816'), so 1815 is the restored Bourbon realm of Naples and Sicily under the name the dossier uses for all of it.

Same outline as 1815-1819. The 1820 revolution forced the king to grant a constitution (13 July) and Austrian forces entered Naples on 24 March 1821, but no territory changed hands (Revolutions of 1820: 'In February 1821, it sent an army to crush the revolution in Naples'), so the shape stands to 1847.

correction.text: the mainland kingdom plus the citadel of Messina, which the Sicilian Parliament never controlled

keyframe_review.note: 69,254 km2: the mainland only, because Sicily was independent from the revolt that 'commenced on 12 January 1848' and 'resulted in an independent state'. The page says the Sicilian Parliament 'was never able to control the well fortified city of Messina', so Messina's citadel stayed Bourbon and is added back. Cliopatria's 'Italian Nationalists' 1848 shape covers Sicily (75 of its 76 cells lie in the Two Sicilies' 1849 outline).

correction.text: unchanged shape; Sicily comes back to the Bourbons on 15 May 1849, not on 1 January

keyframe_review.note: 91,430 km2: Cliopatria returns Sicily on 1 January 1849, but the page has the Bourbon army 'taking back full control of the island on 15 May 1849 by force' and the revolutionary government lasting 'from 12 January 1848 to 15 May 1849'. The shape is right from 15 May 1849 to 1859; until then Sicily is rebel-held. The shape is given unchanged; the ledger's gain of 15 May carries the date.

56,554 km2: the mainland without Sicily and Calabria, the kingdom as it stood after Garibaldi 'disembarked in Calabria' on 19 August 1860 and before the plebiscites of 21 October (Cliopatria's Kingdom of Sardinia 1860 shape, 163,326 km2, holds Sicily and Calabria). It stands as the year's mainland outline; the ledger carries the dated steps (Marsala 11 May, Palermo 6 June, Milazzo 1 August, Calabria 19 August, Naples in September, plebiscite 21 October, Gaeta 13 February 1861). Infobox 1860: 111,900 km2, so this shape is 0.5 of it, as expected for a partly conquered kingdom.

union.text: the fortress of Gaeta and its district
the fortress of Civitella del Tronto

correction.text: Gaeta, Civitella del Tronto and the citadel of Messina, the three strongholds the kingdom still held in 1861

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1861, which Cliopatria lacks: after the plebiscites the kingdom held only Gaeta ('the capitulation was signed on 13 February' 1861), the citadel of Messina (capitulated with Gaeta on 17 March according to the Expedition page) and Civitella del Tronto ('the last organized centre of resistance', surrendered 20 March 1861). The Kingdom of Sardinia's 1861 shape covers the rest.

region.text: the mainland kingdom and Sicily, restored to the Bourbons

ledger.note: 1815: the Bourbons are restored to Naples and Sicily. Infobox 'Bourbon Restoration: 20 May 1815'; the dated name 'Two Sicilies' follows on 8 December 1816. The page does not give the Treaty of Casalanza date; the region is the mainland and Sicily.
1816: the court moves to Palermo (infobox 'Palermo (1816-1817)'), going back to Naples in 1817 ('Naples (1817-1861)').

1816: the Kingdoms of Naples and Sicily become one, the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies. Infobox 'Founded: 8 December 1816'; 'In 1816 he annulled the constitution and Sicily became fully reintegrated into the new state'.
1817: the seat returns to Naples (infobox 'Naples (1817-1861)'; the page does not give the move itself).

region.text: the island of Sicily except the fortress of Messina

ledger.note: 1848: Sicily rebels and becomes independent. 'this final one, which commenced on 12 January 1848, resulted in an independent state'; the revolution began in Palermo and spread across the island, but 'the Sicilian Parliament was never able to control the well fortified city of Messina'.

1849: the Bourbon army retakes Sicily. 'the Bourbon army taking back full control of the island on 15 May 1849 by force', ending the provisional government 'from 12 January 1848 to 15 May 1849'. The page gives no separate date for Palermo.

1860: Garibaldi lands at Marsala. 'Garibaldi's landing in Marsala on 11 May 1860'; the 'first clash on 15 May 1860 in the battle of Calatafimi'. The conquering side is Garibaldi's volunteers acting for Piedmont; Cliopatria gives Sicily to the Kingdom of Sardinia in 1860, so that is the counterpart.

region.text: Sicily except the citadel of Messina

ledger.note: 1860: Sicily falls, bar Messina's citadel. 'On 6 June the Bourbon troops defending the Sicilian capital capitulated'; at Milazzo the attack began on 20 July and 'the Bourbon commander surrendered on 1 August'. The citadel of Messina held out to March 1861.

region.text: Sicily except the citadel of Messina

ledger.note: 1860: the fighting for Sicily ends with the surrender at Milazzo on 1 August, and the crossing to the mainland follows.

region.text: Calabria, the toe of the Italian peninsula

ledger.note: 1860: Garibaldi crosses to the mainland. 'On 19 August Garibaldi's men disembarked in Calabria'.

region.text: Calabria, the toe of the Italian peninsula

ledger.note: 1860: Calabria falls to Garibaldi. 'On 19 August Garibaldi's men disembarked in Calabria'; Reggio was 'conquered at high cost by Nino Bixio on 21 August', and 'On 30 August the Bourbon army, commanded by General Giuseppe Ghio, was disarmed in Soveria Mannelli and surrendered without a fight'. Cliopatria's Sardinia 1860 shape holds Calabria and the Two Sicilies 1860 shape does not. [Reviewer eu-20-k, 2026-10-31: corrected on the Expedition of the Thousand page.] Was September, confidence 1.

region.text: Calabria, the toe of the Italian peninsula

ledger.note: 1860: the Calabrian campaign ends with the surrender at Soveria Mannelli: 'On 30 August the Bourbon army ... was disarmed in Soveria Mannelli and surrendered without a fight'; Naples was entered on 7 September. [Reviewer eu-20-k, 2026-10-31: corrected on the Expedition of the Thousand page.] Was September, confidence 1.

union.text: the fortress of Gaeta and its district
the fortress of Civitella del Tronto

region.text: the mainland provinces except the fortresses of Gaeta and Civitella del Tronto

ledger.note: 1860: the mainland is annexed to Piedmont-Sardinia. After the Battle of the Volturno, 'the rest of the Piedmontese Army crossed the Two Sicilies frontier'; 'A few days later (21 October) a plebiscite confirmed the annexation'. Gaeta, Civitella del Tronto and Messina's citadel still held out.

region.text: the fortress of Gaeta and its district

ledger.note: 1861: Gaeta capitulates. 'the capitulation was signed on 13 February' (the Expedition page gives 17 March 1861 for Gaeta and Messina together, which conflicts); the first Piedmontese infantry entered a day later.

1861: the citadel of Messina capitulates. 'the capitulations of the fortresses of Gaeta and Messina on 17 March 1861' (the same page also gives 13 February for the end of the siege of Gaeta, and the Gaeta page confirms 13 February).

region.text: the fortress of Civitella del Tronto

ledger.note: 1861: Civitella del Tronto, 'the last organized centre of resistance', surrenders on 20 March 1861.

region.text: the fortress of Civitella del Tronto

ledger.note: 1861: the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies ends. 'The Kingdom of Two Sicilies ended some days later' than the capitulation of Gaeta (13 February), when Civitella del Tronto surrendered on 20 March 1861; the Kingdom of Italy had been proclaimed on 17 March 1861 (Two Sicilies infobox).

wars.name: Revolutions of 1820 (Neapolitan revolution and Austrian intervention)
wars.outcome: The king granted a constitution (13 July 1820); the Holy Alliance 'decided in October 1820 to intervene', an Austrian army was sent in February 1821 and entered Naples on 24 March 1821, and the Carbonari revolts collapsed. No territory changed.
wars.note: The Austrian garrison that stayed after 1821 is not dated by any page opened; no occupation event is written.

wars.name: Sicilian revolution of 1848
wars.outcome: Sicily was an independent state from 12 January 1848 until the Bourbon army retook the island by force on 15 May 1849.
wars.note: Cliopatria's 'Italian Nationalists' row is 1848 only; the revolt lasted to May 1849.

wars.name: Expedition of the Thousand
wars.outcome: Garibaldi landed at Marsala (11 May 1860), took Palermo (6 June), Milazzo (1 August), crossed to Calabria (19 August) and entered Naples (September); the plebiscite of 21 October confirmed the annexation to Piedmont-Sardinia.
wars.note: Fortress capitulations of 13 February to 20 March 1861 end the kingdom.

wars.name: Siege of Gaeta (1860-1861)

zones.text: the fortress of Gaeta and its district

wars.outcome: The siege 'started on 5 November 1860' (range 5-12 November); the capitulation was signed on 13 February 1861 and Civitella del Tronto surrendered on 20 March 1861, which ended the kingdom.
wars.note: Francis II and his wife surrendered at Gaeta.

certainty.note: A kingdom with an established land frontier with the Papal States and the sea elsewhere; no page opened dates a survey, so this is the administrative frontier of the restored realm.
The front lines of Garibaldi's advance and the beleaguered fortresses are approximate.

notes:
Page budget 5 used (Two Sicilies, Expedition of the Thousand, Sicilian revolution of 1848, Revolutions of 1820, Siege of Gaeta).
START. The state is the Bourbon realm restored on 20 May 1815 (Kingdom of Naples plus Sicily); the name 'Two Sicilies' dates from 8 December 1816. The dossier starts in 1815 to match Cliopatria and treats 1816 as a rename. Predecessors: kingdom-of-naples-napoleonic (mainland) and kingdom-of-naples-bourbon (Sicily).
END. Cliopatria ends in 1860; the page-dated end is 1861 (Gaeta 13 February, Civitella del Tronto 20 March, Messina citadel 17 March), so a one-year rump keyframe is added for 1861 and the 1860 shape (mainland without Sicily and Calabria) is left to the dated ledger events. The Kingdom of Sardinia's Cliopatria shapes 1860 (163,326 km2) and 1861 (235,522 km2) already hold the south.
ITALIAN NATIONALISTS. Cliopatria's 'Italian Nationalists' row (1848, 21,788 km2) is Sicily (75 of 76 cells lie in the Two Sicilies' 1849 outline). The revolt lasted to 15 May 1849, so the 1849 Cliopatria shape returns Sicily four and a half months early; the counterpart in the ledger is 'italian-nationalists'.
GARIBALDI 1860. The counterpart for the 1860 losses is kingdom-of-sardinia (Cliopatria assigns Sicily and Calabria to it in 1860); Garibaldi's dictatorship held Sicily and the south for about five months and has no dossier or row. Calabria fell in August 1860 (landing 19 August, Reggio 21 August, surrender at Soveria Mannelli 30 August, Expedition page); the loss is dated August at confidence 2 (reviewer eu-20-k correction; the draft had September at confidence 1).
NOT RECORDED. The Austrian occupation army after March 1821 (no page opened dates its end); the constitution of 13 July 1820; Murat's landing in Calabria in October 1815 (one sentence, no outcome). Benevento and Pontecorvo (papal enclaves) are not on the pages. The 1849-1859 shape and the 1815-1847 shape are Cliopatria's and stand.
Gazetteer names the gazetteer lacks: Gaeta, Civitella del Tronto.
